title_clean: The Shorter Series of Questions and Answers — Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma continues exploring the profound dialogue between Dhammadinnā and Visākha on feelings, underlying tendencies, and the limits of conceptual understanding.
description_long:
Bhante Bodhidhamma continues his exploration of the Cūḷavedalla Sutta (MN 44), focusing on the latter sections of this remarkable discourse between the fully awakened bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā and her former husband Visākha, now a non-returner. This talk examines the cessation of feeling and perception (saññāvedayitanirodha) — an extraordinary meditative attainment available only to non-returners and arahants after mastering all eight jhānas.

The discussion moves through the three types of feeling (vedanā) — pleasant, painful, and neutral — and their underlying tendencies (anusaya): excitement (rāga) for pleasant feelings, aversion for painful ones, and ignorance for neutral feelings. Bhante explains how these tendencies don't always arise, especially in skilled practitioners who can experience equanimity with all feelings. The talk concludes with the profound recognition that conceptual questioning has limits — ultimately, direct practice leading to nibbāna transcends intellectual understanding.

This teaching offers practical insights for meditators on recognizing feelings without reactive tendencies, while honoring the extraordinary attainments possible through dedicated practice.
